# The Lexicon of Restorative Agrisolar Design {.unnumbered}

### A shared design language for agrisolar photovoltaic landscapes


Draft

Agrisolar already has communities. Solar graziers, extension agents, agrivoltaic researchers,
community-solar developers, farmland-protection advocates, conservation biologists, hydrologists,
and county planners have each built real practice around their part of the problem. What they do
not have is a vocabulary that crosses between them — the terms were built separately, so the parts
do not compose. What is missing is not a community; it is a shared translation layer between the
ones already at work.

This lexicon is descriptive about how sites are built and openly committed about what they are
for. It aims to let two people who have never met describe their sites to each other precisely,
recognize which design problems they share, and locate their genuine disagreements — and it holds,
in its title and throughout, that ecological, hydrological, and community function belong among the
objectives of agrisolar design rather than among its accidents.

---

## Start here

**If you have land in mind and want to know what is possible on it**, go straight to
[what appears at each scale](chapters/6-archetypes.qmd#sec-by-zone) — the forms that recur at each
size of project, from a barn roof to a regional complex, with what each one asks of the ground.

**If you are weighing a specific proposal**, the [design pressures](chapters/3-design-pressures.qmd)
name the forces pulling on it and the conflicts worth arguing about openly.

**If you are trying to pin down a term** someone has used, the
[alphabetical index](chapters/index-alphabetical.qmd) lists everything this document defines.

Everything else is the reasoning behind those three, and reads in order.

---

## How it is organized

Three structural devices carry the document.

**[The Scale Transect](chapters/1-the-scale-transect.qmd)** — a single gradient from
farmstead to regional that most other terms are read against. Scale determines what is physically,
economically, and institutionally possible before design begins.

**[The Sharing–Sparing Axis](chapters/2-the-sharingsparing-axis.qmd)** — whether the
array shares land with production, spares land by taking ground out of it, or neither.

**[Design Pressures](chapters/3-design-pressures.qmd)** — the competing forces every
site must settle. This is where the document takes sides, on purpose — pressures are meant to pull in a direction.

The design templates in circulation are not the object of this lexicon. They are
**[archetypes](chapters/6-archetypes.qmd)** — ways the pressures have been resolved
at particular scales and sharing postures.

In one line: three structural devices (scale, sharing–sparing, pressures) →
**[general terminology](chapters/5-general-terminology.qmd)** →
**[archetypes](chapters/6-archetypes.qmd)** →
**[open issues](chapters/7-open-issues.qmd)**.

To look a term up directly, see the **[Index — Alphabetical](chapters/index-alphabetical.qmd)**;
the built-in search box at the top of every page complements it.

## Status

This is a working draft circulated for comment. Two things in particular are unresolved:

- Several citations are **[not yet verified](chapters/sources.qmd)** and are marked as such.
- The **[open issues](chapters/7-open-issues.qmd)** list records decisions the document
  has deliberately not made.

Corrections, disagreements, and proposed terms are welcome as GitHub issues or pull requests.
